query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Substituting conventional EAM references with a deep neural network–based interatomic potential, trained on ab initio liquid configurations of multicomponent HEAs near their melting points, will better capture the configurational diversity of the liquid state. This should lead to improved reference–target phase-space overlap and a measurable reduction in the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to the TOR-TILD EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys (e.g., refractory HEAs such as those containing Hf, Ta, Zr, Ti, Nb) in both the solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures.
generation.intervention: Implement a deep neural network (DNN) interatomic potential as the reference potential during thermodynamic integration, replacing the traditional EAM potential.
generation.conditions: The method applies to HEAs in which the liquid state at temperatures between approximately 0.9 Tm and Tm shows extensive configurational diversity due to multicomponent mixing, particularly in refractory systems where high melting temperatures are reached.
generation.structural_mediator: The DNN potential, by virtue of its many-body representation, mediates an accurate mapping of the complex ab initio energy landscape onto a classical framework, thus bridging the structural variations in the dense liquid state.
generation.mechanism: Because EAM potentials are limited by their simpler functional forms, they cannot adequately represent the vast number of atomic configurations present in the ab initio liquid of complex alloys. The DNN potential, trained to reproduce ab initio data, inherently captures the subtleties of many-body interactions and the variation in local environments. This promotes greater phase-space overlap between the reference and target systems and yields a shorter, less mismatched thermodynamic integration path.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermodynamic integration using the DNN reference will yield free-energy differences with significantly reduced integration path mismatches (i.e. lower error margins) compared to those obtained using TOR-TILD’s EAM references. This improvement will manifest as a more continuous and accurate free-energy profile along the integration path.
generation.baseline: Present approaches using TOR-TILD’s EAM references suffer from significant free-energy integration path mismatches owing to their inability to sample the full configurational space of the ab initio liquid.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective for multicomponent HEAs near their melting temperature, but may be less advantageous in systems with extremely directional bonding or in regimes where ab initio training data is insufficient. Its benefits might diminish outside the near–melting (0.9 Tm to Tm) regime.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative degree of mismatch reduction is uncertain and likely system dependent; while moderate to substantial improvement is anticipated, precise factors will require systematic validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform parallel thermodynamic integration simulations on a selected refractory HEA system near melting temperature. One series of simulations should use the traditional EAM reference (TOR-TILD) and the other should employ the newly developed DNN potential trained on representative ab initio liquid configurations. Compare the integration path errors and the free-energy convergence between the two methods.
measurements: Calculated free-energy differences along the integration path
Phase-space overlap metrics (e.g. distribution similarity between reference and ab initio configurations)
Error margins and convergence rate of the thermodynamic integration
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DNN-based integration does not significantly reduce the free-energy error (i.e. does not show a measurable reduction in path mismatch and improved phase-space overlap relative to the EAM-based integration), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The melting temperature is a crucial property of materials that determines their potential applications in different industrial fields. In this study, we used a deep neural network potential to describe the structure of high-entropy (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x carbonitrides (HECN) in both solid and liquid states. This approach allows us to predict heating and cooling temperatures depending on the nitrogen content to determine the melting temperature and analyze structure changes from atomistic point of view. A steady increase in nitrogen content leads to increasing melting temperature, with a maximum approaching for 25% of nitrogen in the HECN. A careful analysis of pair correlations, together with calculations of entropy in the considered liquid phases of HECNs allows us to explain the origin of the nonlinear enhancement of the melting temperature with increasing nitrogen content. The maximum melting temperature of 3580 ± 30 K belongs to (TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 composition. The improved melting behavior of high-entropy compounds by the addition of nitrogen provides a promising way towards modification of thermal properties of functional and constructional materials.
